# Nested tables in WordprocessingShape text boxes

Original controls generated by `tools/nested_shape_table_fixture.py`, using this
repository's independently authored shape-tables control. No corpus artwork,
third-party engine, or font binary is included. Each of sixteen pages pairs the
same table in the main story and in a standalone WPS text box. Cases vary outer
cell left/right padding, nested cell padding, border thickness, positive and
negative indent, percentage width, and centered/right alignment.

The reference application exported `native.pdf` from `control.docx`.
`tools/record_nested_shape_tables.py` records all 96 named text origins and
SHA-256 hashes. Browser assertions require installed Arial and compare every
origin, including body controls; unit tests also verify immutable layout models
and drawing markup through body editing, export, reopening and exact undo.

The reference application compatibility behavior: an in-flow nested table inside a WPS cell starts
at the parent's leading inner border edge instead of its padded writing origin.
The width available for percentage sizing and alignment remains the padded
writing width. Nested cells retain their own physical margins. The paired main
story tables retain their normal padded origin. This is not a smaller default
cell margin and must not be implemented as a fixed offset.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.4.68 (tcMar), 17.4.41–42 (tblCellMar),
17.4.50 (tblInd), 17.4.28 (jc), and 17.4.87 (table measurements) describe
ordinary cell/table geometry. They do not expressly specify this WPS origin
exception. These controls document reference-specific behavior beyond uniformly
padded placement, rather than claiming a normative contradiction about text
margins. Floating nested tables remain unsupported within retained WPS text.
This fixture does not certify every nesting depth or bidirectional table mode.
